The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.

why: The statement is a single universal yes/no over all groups, so one group with an injective non-surjective cellular automaton over a finite alphabet answers it in full. openai-math-197 claims exactly that: a group algebra K[G] over a finite field with ab=1, ba≠1, and the standard transfer (b gives an injective CA on K^G, not surjective since ba≠1) — consistent with the published fact that surjunctive groups have stably finite group rings (ceccherini-2023). So it is scope whole, direction refuted, object a counterexample; it is unreviewed (8 days old, only a Lean build with sorry status unknown and no human reader). I kept it credible: there is no specific error, and the non-executed search prescription is a termination/existence argument, not a gap; but it is a landmark claim resting only on machine checking. AI role generated, from the repository's statement that results were obtained by the internal model. The Astra non-sofic result and its human follow-ups (Fournier-Facio, Kun-Thom) concern soficity, not surjunctivity — non-sofic does not imply non-surjunctive and the chapter lists this group's surjunctivity as open — so they are variants; Bowen-Chapman (IRSs) and the 2024 monoid paper likewise. Pre-snapshot class results (sofic, residually finite, amenable) are cases; the undated Lawton and amenable entries are placed before the snapshot because the record cites them in a 2010 book. Cannizzo and Shahryari are withdrawn.
doubts: openai-math-197 is 8 days old with no human engagement; the README quote is a blanket statement about 'the vast majority of results' rather than this result specifically, and no individual human authors are named. The Lean scope covers the direct-finiteness counterexamples and, for the odd-characteristic case, states the CA is injective but not surjective; whether its definitions match the standard ones was not audited. A Kaplansky direct-finiteness counterexample would itself imply a non-sofic group, so this claim is consistent with the Astra event but makes a much stronger assertion; readers should treat it as a claimed refutation pending expert review.
